lonchidionoides:study:1.title: A new genus of lonchidiid hybodontiform sharks from the Cretaceous of North Africa and South America (Geological Magazine, 2026)

lonchidionoides:abstract:1.title: A new genus of lonchidiid hybodontiform sharks from the Cretaceous of North Africa and South America (abstract)

facts.statement: The taxon Lonchidionoides was formally named by Vullo et al. in 2026.
Lonchidionoides belongs to the extinct hybodont family Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Lonchidionoides is an extinct genus of hybodont in the family Lonchidiidae.

facts.statement: Lonchidionoides trifurcatum is known from the latest Albian–early Cenomanian Tiout Formation of Algeria.
facts.quote: known from the 'mid'-Cretaceous (latest Albian–early Cenomanian ages) Tiout Formation of Algeria

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Lonchidionoides have also been found in the Barremian–Aptian Quiricó Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: Teeth of this genus are also known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian–Aptian ages) Quiricó Formation of Brazil

facts.statement: Romain Vullo and colleagues described Lonchidionoides trifurcatum in 2026 based on five teeth from the Tiout Formation in northern Algeria.
facts.quote: In 2026, Romain Vullo and colleagues described Lonchidionoides trifurcatum as a new genus and species of lonchidiid hybodont based on five teeth from the Tiout Formation ('Garet El Hemmam' locality) of Laghouat Province, northern Algeria.

facts.statement: The generic name Lonchidionoides refers to its similarity to the teeth of the genus Lonchidion.
facts.quote: The generic name, Lonchidionodes, derives from its similarity to the teeth of Lonchidion

facts.statement: The specific epithet trifurcatum describes the trident‑like shape of the anterior teeth.
facts.quote: The specific name, trifurcatum, refers to the trident-like morphology of the anterior dentition.

facts.statement: Nine isolated teeth from Brazil were initially described as ?Lonchidiidae in 2021 and remain as Lonchidionoides sp. pending further material.
facts.quote: Nine isolated teeth from the Early Cretaceous Quiricó Formation ('Fazenda Tereza' locality) were initially described as ?Lonchidiidae in 2021. These are nearly identical in morphology and size to L. trifurcatum, but remain in open nomenclature as L. sp.

facts.statement: Lonchidionoides has a heterodont dentition with tricuspid anterior teeth and larger crushing posterior teeth, while lateral teeth are intermediate in form.
The genus is interpreted as a non‑marine hybodontiform, indicating a large ancestral distribution that was split by the opening of the South Atlantic.
The description of Lonchidionoides was published in Geological Magazine in 2026.

rejected.statement: Lonchidionoides is a valid genus and species of hybodont shark described in 2026.
The genus contains a single named species, Lonchidionoides trifurcatum.
rejected.quote: The genus contains a single named species, Lonchidionoides trifurcatum
